satellites.description: UK Statutory Sick Pay (April 2026 rules), Maternity Pay and National Living Wage from gov.uk.
knows: From 6 April 2026 the Employment Rights Act 2025 (ss.10 and 11, commenced by SI 2026/373) removed the 3 SSP waiting days and the lower earnings limit. SSP is now the lower of £123.25 a week or 80% of average weekly earnings, paid from the first qualifying day.
Before 6 April 2026 SSP was £118.75 flat, needed earnings of at least £125 a week and 4 days of sickness in a row, and the first 3 qualifying days were unpaid.
HMRC's 2026/27 SSP day tables round the unrounded daily rate times days up to the next penny, so 4 days on a 6-day week is £82.17.
The 2026/27 family pay flat rate is £194.32 (2025/26: £187.18). The SMP rate changed on Sunday 5 April 2026, so a maternity pay period that crosses April uses both.
The lower earnings limit for maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental pay is £129 a week in 2026/27 (£125 in 2025/26).
The National Living Wage is £12.71 an hour from 1 April 2026, with £10.85 for 18 to 20 and £8 for under 18s and apprentices. The April 2027 rates are already published: £13.21, £11.27 and £8.31.

tools.name: calculate_statutory_sick_pay
tools.description: Works out UK Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) for a period of sickness. Knows the Employment Rights Act 2025 changes in force from 6 April 2026: SSP is paid from the first qualifying day (no 3 waiting days), the lower earnings limit is gone, and the weekly rate is the lower of £123.25 or 80% of average weekly earnings. For sickness starting 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026 it applies the old rules (£118.75 flat, £125 lower earnings limit, 3 waiting days, 4-day period of incapacity) and flags the SI 2026/373 transitional rules. Uses HMRC's unrounded daily rates and 28-week cap. Rates fetched from gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-02.

tools.name: calculate_statutory_maternity_pay
tools.description: Works out UK Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) week by week for 39 weeks: 90% of average weekly earnings for 6 weeks, then the lower of the flat rate or 90% for 33 weeks. Flat rate £187.18 from 6 April 2025 and £194.32 from 5 April 2026, switching for pay weeks that start after the April uprating. Finds the expected week of childbirth, the qualifying week (15th week before), the latest employment start date for 26 weeks' service and the lower earnings limit for that week (£125 in 2025/26, £129 in 2026/27). Same structure applies to Statutory Adoption Pay. Figures from gov.uk, fetched 2026-11-02.

tools.name: get_minimum_wage_rates
tools.description: Returns the UK National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage hourly rates in force on a date, by age band and apprentice rate, and the rate that applies to a given age. Holds April 2024, April 2025, April 2026 (£12.71 for 21 and over, £10.85 for 18 to 20, £8 under 18 and apprentices) and the published April 2027 rates (£13.21, £11.27, £8.31). Can also give weekly and annual pay at the rate for given hours. Rates fetched from gov.uk on 2026-11-02.

tools.name: check_eligibility
tools.description: Checks the qualifying conditions for UK Statutory Sick Pay, Maternity, Paternity, Adoption or Shared Parental Pay and returns each condition as met, not met or not checkable, plus the weekly amounts. Knows that from 6 April 2026 SSP has no earnings threshold and no waiting days, and applies the 26 weeks' continuous employment test into the qualifying week (15th week before the due week, or the matching week for adoption) and the lower earnings limit (£125 in 2025/26, £129 in 2026/27). Data from gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk, fetched 2026-11-02.

example.prompt: An employee on 400 pounds a week is off sick for 10 working days from 4 May 2026. How much Statutory Sick Pay is due?
example.summary:
Under the 2026/27 rules SSP is £123.25 a week (flat weekly rate). For 10 qualifying days off on a 5-day week, 10 days are payable from day one: total £246.50.

Estimate from gov.uk rates, not legal or payroll advice. Check special cases with HMRC or the gov.uk calculators.

satellites.description: Exact U.S. federal holidays and business days 1971-2100, OPM and Federal Reserve observance.
knows: The observance rule. A Saturday holiday is observed on Friday by federal employees (5 U.S.C. 6103(b)). A Sunday holiday is observed on Monday (E.O. 11582). The Friday can fall in the previous year.

The Federal Reserve rule is different. When a holiday falls on Saturday, Reserve Banks are open on Friday (K.8). So 2026-07-03 is a federal holiday but a banking day. Use `calendar: "fed_banking"` for ACH, wire and settlement dates.
The rule history. Juneteenth from 2021. MLK Day from 1986. Veterans Day was the fourth Monday in October from 1971 to 1977.
Inauguration Day. It applies only to DC-area federal employees, every four years. It moves to Monday when January 20 is a Sunday and has no substitute day when it is a Saturday (2029).
All 212 holiday rows in OPM's published tables for 2011-2030 match this server's output. A test checks this.

tools.name: list_federal_holidays
tools.description: Exact U.S. federal holidays for any year 1971-2100 under 5 U.S.C. 6103: legal date, OPM observed date (Saturday -> Friday, Sunday -> Monday, so New Year's Day 2022 is observed Friday 2021-12-31) and the Federal Reserve closure date (Fed Banks stay OPEN the Friday before a Saturday holiday). Applies the rule history a model tends to get wrong: Juneteenth from 2021, MLK Day from 1986, Veterans Day on the 4th Monday of October 1971-1977, and Inauguration Day (DC area only, flagged optional). No network calls.

tools.name: is_business_day
tools.description: Says whether a date (1971-2100) is a business day on the U.S. federal (OPM) calendar or the Federal Reserve banking calendar, names the holiday if any, and returns the previous and next business day. The two calendars differ when a holiday falls on Saturday: 2026-07-03 is a federal holiday but a Fed banking day.

tools.name: add_business_days
tools.description: Adds (or with a negative number subtracts) N business days to a date, skipping weekends and observed U.S. federal or Federal Reserve holidays exactly. The start date is not counted. With 0, returns the start date if it is a business day, otherwise the next one. Lists every holiday skipped.

tools.name: count_business_days
tools.description: Counts business days between two dates (1971-2100) on the U.S. federal or Federal Reserve calendar, excluding weekends and observed holidays. include_start and include_end default to true, like Excel NETWORKDAYS. If end is before start the count is negative. Lists the weekday holidays that were excluded.

tools.name: invoice_due_date
tools.description: Computes an invoice due date from an issue date and net terms in calendar days (Net 30 = 30), then optionally rolls a weekend or U.S. holiday due date: following (next business day), preceding, or modified_following (next business day unless it crosses into the next month). Uses exact observed federal or Federal Reserve holidays.

example.prompt: How many business days are there from December 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027, excluding US federal holidays?
example.summary: There are 32 business days from 2026-12-01 to 2027-01-15 (start included, end included) on the federal calendar: 46 calendar days, 12 weekend days. Excluded weekday holidays: 2026-12-25 Christmas Day; 2027-01-01 New Year's Day.

satellites.description: Today's UV Index forecast by US ZIP code or city, with hourly peak and UV Alert, from EPA and NWS.
knows: Today's UV Index for your ZIP code. It changes every day with season, cloud cover and ozone, so a model's training data cannot know it.
The hour when the sun is strongest today and the hours when EPA says protection is needed.
Whether NWS and EPA have issued a UV Alert for the place today.

tools.name: get_uv_index_today
tools.description: Today's UV Index forecast for a US ZIP code or city and state, read now from EPA (the NWS daily forecast). Returns the UV Index, the EPA category and sun protection advice, whether a UV Alert is in effect, the hourly peak and the local hours when UV is 3 or higher. Your training data cannot know today's UV Index.

tools.name: get_uv_index_hourly
tools.description: Hour by hour UV Index forecast for a US ZIP code or city and state, in the local time of that place, read now from EPA. Returns each hour with its EPA band, the peak hour and the window when UV is 3 or higher. Use it for "when is the sun strongest today" and "what time is safe to be outside" questions.

tools.name: explain_uv_index
tools.description: What a UV Index number means on the EPA scale (0 to 2 Low, 3 to 7 Moderate to High, 8 and above Very High to Extreme) and the EPA sun protection advice for it, plus the NWS UV Alert rule. No network call.

example.prompt: What is the UV Index today in Miami, ZIP 33101?

satellites.description: Vegetable and fruit yield percentage, trim waste and how much produce to buy, from USDA refuse data.
knows: The USDA trim loss for each item, and what it is. Corn on the cob is 36% edible (35% husk, silk and trimmings, 29% cob). Pineapple is 51% (8% core, 16% crown, 26% parings). Cauliflower is 39%, leeks 44%, asparagus 53%, bananas 64%, onions 90%, cucumbers 97%.
USDA household weights for the edible part. A medium onion (2-1/2 inch) is 110 g and a cup of chopped onion is 160 g, so 2 cups chopped needs about 3 medium onions and 356 g as bought.
The difference between as purchased and edible portion. Recipe costing, food cost and portion planning need both. The tools return both, plus the waste.

tools.name: get_vegetable_yield
tools.description: USDA edible yield percent for a raw vegetable or fruit (the share left after removing peel, seeds, core, stems and trimmings), the refuse percent and what the refuse is, plus USDA household weights (1 medium, 1 cup chopped, 1 clove) and the as-purchased weight of one whole item. From USDA SR28 refuse data.

tools.name: calculate_edible_weight
tools.description: Edible weight and trim waste from a purchased (as purchased, untrimmed) weight of a raw vegetable or fruit, using the USDA edible yield percent.

tools.name: calculate_amount_to_buy
tools.description: How much of a raw vegetable or fruit to buy for a recipe amount. Give the prepared amount in g, kg, oz or lb, or as a USDA household measure such as "cup chopped", "cup sliced", "medium" or "clove". Returns the edible weight needed, the as-purchased weight to buy at the USDA edible yield, and the number of whole items (for example medium onions) to buy.

tools.name: list_vegetable_yields
tools.description: List raw vegetables and fruits with their USDA edible yield percent, filtered to fruit or vegetable and sorted by name, lowest yield or highest yield.

example.prompt: How many onions do I need to buy for 3 cups chopped?
example.summary: For 3 x cup, chopped (160 g each, USDA) of onions, raw you need 480 g edible, so buy about 533 g (1.18 lb) as purchased at the USDA edible yield of 90%, or about 4.4 x medium (2-1/2" dia) (round up to 5).
